newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Smit Int sells 49 ships to Seacor.
newsitem.headline: Smit Int sells 49 ships to Seacor.

text.p: Shipping Group Smit Internationale said on Monday it had reached agreement on the sale of its fleet of 49 off-shore supply ships to U.S. firm Seacor Holdings Inc.
The Dutch firm said it would receive $84 million, plus 712,000 Seacor shares valued at $35 million and $21 million worth of convertible Seacor bonds.
Smit Internationale said an additional earnings-related payment would be due in 1999, based on the results of the fleet in 1997 and 1998. This would be paid in cash and bonds, it said.
The sale fits in with the firm's strategy of returning to its core business of salvage, transport, offshore, water utilities and harbour towage.
Smit said it was selling all of its 100 percent owned off-shore supply ships and its interests in this sector.
As one of Seacor's biggest shareholders, Smit would gain a seat on the Board of Directors of the company, to be renamed Smit-Seacor, Smit said.
"If our fleet performs as we expect over the next two years, we will gain an added bonus in the form of the back-payment," Smit said in a statement.
The transaction is to be completed by December 1996.
Smit, specialised in salvage worldwide, has a fleet of around 300 vessels and employs 2,400 people.
In 1995 turnover amounted to 450 million guilders and net profits 21 million guilders.
Over the first six months of 1996, Smit's net profit rose to 10.6 million guilders from 9.8 million in the same 1995 period.
Dutch shipping and road transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd Group NV holds a stake of 40 percent in Smit Int.
Seacor and its units employ 1,500 staff, with a fleet of 260 vessels.
During the first six months of 1996 Seacor booked turnover of $102 million and profits of $13 million.
